Title: The Free Leg That Looks Good Is the One That Ruins the Turn
Description: Turning on one skate, the free leg wants to swing out behind you. It looks good, and it is the mistake. Bring that skate in against your standing leg instead, and keep your hips level. If one hip has to sit off, let it be the free side sitting higher, never lower. A dropped hip twists your pelvis out of line, and the turn stops before it starts. Quad technique, from Najete Kada. Title: There Are Four One-Foot Turns, Not One
Description: Right skate turning right, right skate turning left, left skate turning right, left skate turning left. Four of them, and most skaters only ever practise the one that feels natural. Pick your favourite to build confidence, then drill all four, because the day the pavement decides which way you go, you want to already own that direction. Quad technique, from Najete Kada. Title: Going Faster Makes the One-Foot Turn Easier
Description: This sounds wrong, and it is not. The faster you roll, the more balance you carry, so a one-foot turn taken with speed is steadier than the same turn crawled through. The catch is everything above your knees: more speed asks for a more solid body, arms out to either side, shoulder blades drawn together, and the skate locked once you have come round. Quad technique, from Najete Kada. Illustration generated with AI.

Title: You Learn to Jump Without Moving an Inch
Description: Before you ever leave the ground, you lift your heels. Standing still, knees bent, stomach in, eyes ahead — raise both heels onto your front wheels and set them back down, over and over, on a beat. That drill is already the jump. It teaches your quads the work and your ankles the balance while the floor is still doing nothing at all. Quad technique, from Najete Kada. Illustration generated with AI.

Title: The Bend Is What Jumps You, Not the Push
Description: One and two: one, you bend; two, you push. The push takes all the credit and the bend does the work, because without rhythm in the flexion there is nothing for the extension to release. Add your arms and it doubles — they swing back as you bend and come forward as you push. Then land on both skates and set up the next one. Quad technique, from Najete Kada. Title: Roller Dance Starts With a Bounce, Not a Step
Description: Before any step at all, you find the beat with your knees. Straighten, bend, straighten, bend, weight on the front of your skates and hips forward. That is the bounce, and it comes first because every roller dance step is counted off it. Faster track, faster bounce. Once it holds, let one skate reach out and come back on the count. Quad technique, from Najete Kada. Illustration generated with AI.

Title: The Dribble Only Works on Your Front Wheels
Description: Skates open, skates close, on the beat: that is the dribble done flat on the floor, and it stays where it is. The version that actually travels is a different animal. Lift your heels slightly, let each skate roll on its front wheels alone, then pivot and swap. It is small and subtle, and it is the sensation that unlocks the step. Quad technique, from Najete Kada. Title: The Catwalk Is Just a Crossover Played Fast
Description: It looks like a step of its own and it is not. Lift a skate, set it down in front of the other, let it travel back underneath you — done slowly, that is a walk. Cross the skate over rather than placing it straight, then run exactly the same thing at double speed, and it is a catwalk. Shoulders back, chin up, weight on the front wheels. Quad technique, from Najete Kada. Illustration generated with AI.
Keywords: roller dance, catwalk, crossover, quad skating

Title: The Moonwalk Is One Swap, Made at the Same Instant
Description: This one is quad-only, and the reason is the brake. One skate rolls on its wheels, the other rests on its toe stop. Drag the rolling skate back until it passes the other, and at that moment both change jobs at once — wheels to stop, stop to wheels. That single simultaneous swap is the whole trick and the whole difficulty. Inline skaters, your brake is at the back and this step does not transfer. From Najete Kada. Illustration generated with AI.
Keywords: roller dance, moonwalk on skates, toe stop, quad skating

Title: The Shuffle Is a Wiper Movement, Except Crossed
Description: Skates a little wider than your hips, heels free, weight on the front wheels. Pivot one skate a quarter turn and bring it back — that is the single-skate version, and it comes first. Then do both at once, drawing them inward until one ends up in front of the other, and alternate which one leads. If a skate rolls a bit while you do it, let it roll. Quad technique, from Najete Kada. Illustration generated with AI.
